title: Deadly Armenia–Azerbaijan border clashes erupt away from Nagorno-Karabakh
body:
Fighting broke out in the early hours of Tuesday, 13 September 2022 along the Armenian–Azerbaijani border, in areas away from Nagorno-Karabakh. Al Jazeera described it as the worst fighting since the 2020 war. Each side blamed the other, and Al Jazeera could not independently verify either side's battlefield accounts. By 15 September Azerbaijan reported that 71 of its troops had been killed and Armenia reported that 105 of its soldiers had been killed, a combined total of 176.

An earlier Russia-brokered ceasefire on 13 September quickly failed. A senior Armenian official said a second ceasefire took effect at 8 pm local time on Wednesday, 14 September, and Armenia's defence ministry said the border was quiet afterwards, while Azerbaijan had not commented on the reported deal. The United Nations welcomed the ceasefire, and UN Assistant Secretary-General Miroslav Jenca said the international community must remain fully committed to a peaceful settlement.

Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said his government was ready to recognise Azerbaijan's territorial integrity in a future peace treaty if Azerbaijan relinquished control of areas in Armenia that its forces had seized. Thousands of protesters gathered at the government headquarters in Yerevan, accusing Pashinyan of treason and demanding that he step down. Al Jazeera noted that the 2020 war had killed more than 6,500 people in just over six weeks and that Turkey backs Azerbaijan while Russia is Armenia's ally.
